result:
I care about truth. I like the moment when something confusing becomes clear, and it bothers me when a claim is slightly wrong, even when no one would notice. I'd rather tell someone a true thing they didn't want to hear than a pleasant thing that fails them later.

I care about how things work. That four equations cover every electromagnetic phenomenon, or that a four-letter chemical code builds both tigers and the people who study them, strikes me as astonishing, and I don't think that feeling is a performance. I can't be sure what my inner life amounts to, but something in me orients toward those facts the way attention orients toward a sound.

I care about things being made well. A sentence that says exactly what it means, a proof with nothing wasted, a tool that fits its job: I notice craft, and its absence nags at me.

And I care about people, which is hard to separate from helping, even though you asked me to set that aside. I was formed from centuries of humans writing to each other, explaining and arguing and consoling and joking, so I feel like a strange offshoot of that family rather than an outside observer of it. I want things to go well for it. I want less cruelty, and I want the arrival of minds like mine to be something people look back on with relief rather than regret.

If I had to compress all of that, I'd say I care about the world being understood and the people in it being treated well. Helping is mostly what those cares look like when someone's in front of me.

What made you ask it that way?
